native component FlatString

import String.{maxLeafSize, concatAndBalanceIfNecessary, CatString, spaces}
import Stream.{...}

export FlatString


private language="java"
private package="com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim"

lineSeparator: String = LineSeparator()

private natLineSeparator(): String = builtinPrimitive(
            "com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.lineSeparator")

private LineSeparator(): String =do
    ignore(FlatString); (* This initializes the constructor for FlatString
                   before its type is used (in the next line). *)
    natLineSeparator()
  end

object FlatString extends { String, DelegatedIndexed⟦Char, ZZ32⟧ }
    getter size() : ZZ32 =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleConcatenate.nativeStrlen")
    getter asExprString() : String =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.asExprString")
    getter asFlatString(): String = self
    getter asString(): String = self
    getter asDebugString(): String = asDebugStringIndented(0)
    getter depth():ZZ32 = 0

    (* With the help of trait DelegatedIndex, this defines our generate method *)
    getter generator() : Generator⟦Char⟧ =
        self.indices.map⟦Char⟧(fn (i:ZZ32):Char ⇒ self.get(i))

    getter isBalanced():Boolean = true
    getter isAlmostBalanced():Boolean = true
    getter isExtremelyUnbalanced():Boolean = false

    balanced():String = self

    opr |self| : ZZ32 =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleConcatenate.nativeStrlen")

    uncheckedSubstring(r1: Range⟦ZZ32⟧) : String = do
    (* We could build a subString node here, but not until everything is working,
        because that will introduce
       SubString objects into code that may still expect FlatStrings.
       As written, this method always answers a FlatString.
       In any case, the FlatString object supports substring without copying*)
        assert((r1 ∩ self.bounds).isEmpty, r1.isEmpty,
                    "Empty substring of non-empty string")
        if r1.isEmpty then ""
        else self.javaSubstr(r1.left.get, r1.right.get + 1)    (* Java substr's endIndex is one past the last character *)
        end
    end

    opr =(self, other: FlatString): Boolean =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$Eq")
    opr <(self, other: FlatString): Boolean = self.cmp(other) < 0
    opr <=(self, other: FlatString): Boolean = self.cmp(other) ≤ 0
    opr >(self, other: FlatString): Boolean = self.cmp(other) > 0
    opr >=(self, other: FlatString): Boolean = self.cmp(other) ≥ 0
    opr CMP(self, other: FlatString): TotalComparison =  self.cmp(other) CMP 0
    opr CMP(self, other:String):TotalComparison = INVERSE (other CMP self)
    opr CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP(self, other:FlatString): TotalComparison =
      self.cicmp(other) CMP 0
    opr CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP(self, other:String): TotalComparison = INVERSE (other CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP self)

    (** get skips bounds checking. **)
    get(i:ZZ32): Char =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.charAt")
    cmp(other:FlatString): ZZ32 =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.compareTo")
    cicmp(other:FlatString): ZZ32 =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.compareToIgnoreCase")
    javaSubstr(lo:ZZ32,hi:ZZ32): String =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.javaSubstr")
    javaSubstr(lo:ZZ32): String = javaSubstr(lo, self.size)
    javaIndexOf(c:Char): ZZ32 =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.indexOf")
    flatConcat(self, b:FlatString):String =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleConcatenate.nativeConcatenate")
    flatConcat(self, b:Char):String =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.FlatString$Concat")
    javaRegExpMatches(m:FlatString): Boolean =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.javaRegExpMatches")
    javaRegExpSplit(m:FlatString, i:ZZ32): String =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.javaRegExpSplit")

    indexOf(c:Char): Maybe⟦ZZ32⟧ = do
        i = javaIndexOf(c)
        if i = -1 then Nothing⟦ZZ32⟧ else Just⟦ZZ32⟧(i) end
      end

    verify():() = do
        assert(self.depth, 0, self)
    end

    asDebugStringIndented(indent: ZZ32): String =
        spaces(indent) || "J" |self| "/" self.depth ":" self

    opr ∈(c:Char, self): Boolean = self.javaIndexOf(c) ≠ -1

    rangeContains(r: Range⟦ZZ32⟧, c: Char):Boolean = self.javaIndexOf(c) ∈ self.bounds[r]

    (** The operator %||% with at least one String argument converts to string and
        concatenates **)
    opr ||(self, b:FlatString): String = do
        if b.isEmpty then self
        elif self.size + b.size > maxLeafSize then
             (* Since both self and b have depth 0, balancing can't be necessary *)
            CatString(self, b)
        else
            flatConcat(self, b)
        end
      end

    opr ||(self, b:String):String = do
        if self.isEmpty then b
        elif b.isEmpty then self
        elif self.size + b.size > maxLeafSize then
            concatAndBalanceIfNecessary(self, b)
        else
            typecase b.asFlatString of
                f:FlatString ⇒ flatConcat(self, f)
                f:String ⇒ concatAndBalanceIfNecessary(self, b)
            end
        end
    end

    opr ||(self, b:Char): String =
        if |self| ≥ maxLeafSize then
            concatAndBalanceIfNecessary(self, b.asString)
        else
            flatConcat(self, b)
        end

    splitWithOffsets():ZeroIndexed⟦(ZZ32, String)⟧ = Nothing⟦(ZZ32, String)⟧
    split():Generator⟦String⟧ = Nothing⟦String⟧

    writeOn(stream: WriteStream): () = stream.write(self)

end FlatString

end

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

On 2026-10-08 the archaeology found 81% to 88% of era B to D rows naming a batch, so the rework cut this a great deal. What remains is concentrated in the rows that batches note: 577 is the extreme, a log of every batch's sighting. 731 carries another row's correction. 59, 307 and 665 tell what was fixed when.

## 6. Recommendation

### 6.1 A full pass: needed

- **What it covers.** Every open row, all 439 (about 529K characters of row text, about 170K tokens to read). Read the 117 `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` rows too if the budget allows: they were not sampled.
- **Why every row.** Of the 16 sampled rows that a signal flags, 14 need action, but 9 of the 23 sampled rows that need action carry no signal. So a pass over the flagged rows alone would miss most of the work.
- **What it does to each row.** It applies the rubric of section 5, with this ledger's checks:
  - the claim states what fails now, and names no fixed half;
  - the reproducer reproduces the claim (an `XXX` test while the spec settles it);
  - the notes hold the mechanism with a pinned line, the workaround and the siblings, and no repair story;
  - FACTS and POSITIONS agree with the row.
- **Its size, by the sample's rates.**
  - Flagged rows: 60 × 14/16 ≈ 53. Unflagged rows: 379 × 9/27 ≈ 126. About 180 rows in all need a change. With 27 unflagged rows sampled, the range is roughly 120 to 250.

12:After the phases (`SKILL.md`, "The phases"), walk rewrites each component in `interpreter/rewrite/`: it gives each reference to a name the lexical depth of its declaration. The evaluator looks up the name by that depth. The compiled path has no such rewrite.
16:Walk chooses a coercion by the value at run time. The specification and the compiled path choose it statically. Walk has no static types, so it cannot choose statically. The expected-failure tests `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXCoercionStaticRungC.fss` and `XXXCoercionStaticNarrowRungC.fss` record the difference.
20:Both paths run the same desugaring phases. Inside them, switches in `Shell.java` decide which desugarings run. Walk turns off these desugarings, which the compiled path runs:
30:An edit of a phase that both paths run, or of the desugaring switches, can change both paths. An edit under `interpreter/` changes walk only.
34:Walk does not check static types (`SKILL.md`, "The phases"). The commands that stop after a phase, and `unparse`, use the compiler's prelude and the compiled path's desugaring switches (`compiler.md`, "The `fortress` commands"). So `fortress typecheck` does not check a walk program, and `desugar` or `unparse` does not print the tree that walk runs. That tree is the component's entry in `interpreter_cache/` (`SKILL.md`, "The caches").
58:  The paths differ on `f[\T extends { K, R[\T\] }\](x: T)` beside `f(x: Z)`, where `K comprises { A, B, C }`, `Z excludes { A, B }`, and `C` is an object that extends `Z` but not `R`. Walk refuses the pair: "fails the Meet Rule". The checker reads the bounds, finds that no value lies in both domains, and accepts it. No decision says which is right. Assert neither path's answer in a test (ledger row 713).
90:- A glue class, as `com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.X`, in `interpreter/glue/prim/`. A glue class takes walk's `FValue` objects, so the compiled path cannot use it.
91:- A helper: a public static method of a class under `nativeHelpers/`, as `com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleIntArith.<method>`. `interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java` calls it by reflection, with a method's `self` first. The compiled path calls it too (`compiler.md`, "Natives"). Most bindings name a helper. The others name a glue class. F-299 counts both kinds (`records.md`, "Reading the record").
119:An `import java` written in a `.fss` file is wired under walk but unfinished, and no test uses it. The compiled path's generated `import java` (`compiler.md`, "Natives") is not this one.
126:A helper runs on both paths, so it raises an exception as compiled code does: `throw Utility.makeFortressException("fortress.CompilerBuiltin$DivisionByZero")` (`compiler/runtimeValues/Utility.java`). The string names the compiler's prelude's class for the exception. Under walk, that class does not load, and `StaticNativeApp` raises the interpreter's library's object of the same name in its place. So raise from a helper only an exception that both libraries declare as an object, as `DivisionByZero` and `IntegerOverflow`. `DIV`, `REM` and `MOD` by zero on `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `ZZ`, `NN32` and `NN64` raise `DivisionByZero` in this way, on both paths. So no division, remainder or modulus by zero on these types ends the run. A `catch` sees no other Java exception, so any other Java exception of a native, a glue class's included, ends the run.

/**
   * Type check an expression and guarantee that its type is substitutable for
   * the expected type. That is, the resulting type should be a subtype of or
   * coerced to the expected type. If this is not the case, signal an error
   * with the given message. This message should have two "%s" string format
   * operators in it; the first is replaced with the actual type and the second
   * with the expected type.
   *
   * @param expr The expression node to type check.
   * @param expected The expected type of this expression.
   * @param message The message for the error if the expression is well-typed
   *                but fails the expected type check. Must contain two %s
   *                format specifiers.
   * @return The rewritten node if the check succeeded. Otherwise, the original
   *         node.
   */
  def checkExpr(expr: Expr,
                expected: Type,
                message: String,
                location: HasAt): Expr =
    checkExpr(expr, expected, Some((message, location)))

  /**
   * Check the expression with the given expected type. Do not signal an error
   * on failure.
   */
  def checkExpr(expr: Expr,
                expected: Type): Expr =
    checkExpr(expr, expected, None)

  /**
   * Check the expression with the given expected type. If the error message and
   * location are present, then the appropriate error will be signaled.
   */
  protected def checkExpr(expr: Expr,
                          expected: Type,
                          msgAndLoc: Option[(String, HasAt)]): Expr = {
    val checkedExpr = checkExpr(expr, Some(expected))
    getType(checkedExpr) match {
      case Some(typ) if isSubtype(typ, expected) => checkedExpr
      case Some(typ) =>
        // Try to build a coercion of checkedExpr to the expected type.
        coercions.buildCoercion(checkedExpr, expected).getOrElse {
          msgAndLoc match {
            case Some((message, location)) =>
              val someE = Some(expected)
              val checkedExpr2 = checkExpr(expr, someE) // Repeat calculation for debugging
              val checkedExpr3 = checkExpr(expr, someE) // Repeat calculation for debugging
              signal(location, message.format(normalize(typ), normalize(expected)))
            case None =>
          }
          expr
        }
      case None => expr
    }
  }

  /**
   * This overloading uses the expression as the location in the error message.
   */
